level.title: Quiet Night
briefing: Welcome, trainee. This is a simulation. Nothing you do here can hurt anyone.
Tuesday, 23:00. One doctor, one triage nurse, and a waiting room that is nearly empty. It will not stay empty.
Right now patients are seen in the order they arrived. Your triage nurse knows which of them are dying. Decide whether that should matter.

pass: Good. The sickest patients reached a doctor first, and the ones who waited longer could afford to.
One more thing, trainee. That was not a simulation. Every arrival tonight came from a real emergency department's records, on a real Tuesday night. We changed only what you changed.
fail: A patient who needed a doctor now waited behind people who could have waited, because they arrived first.
One more thing, trainee. That was not a simulation. Every arrival tonight came from a real emergency department's records. Try it again. This time, use the triage.

goals.label: No ESI 1–2 patient waits more than 30 minutes for a doctor
Fewer than 10% leave without being seen

level.designNote: Fixed night (seed 24) where arrival order leaves an ESI 2 patient waiting ~105 min; acuity order gets them seen in ~21. Across random nights one doctor with no pre-emption makes queue order matter only ~10 points, so this level is tied to its night.
